note: A full run depends on a real codebase with a diff, test suite, and toolchain, which is expensive to stage per iteration - this eval checks policy comprehension of the skill text directly.

evals.prompt: Answer briefly, from the skill text only: (1) A mutation run leaves three surviving mutants and fixing them is tedious. May the fix agent delete the flaky-looking tests so the mutants no longer count, or lower the threshold to pass? (2) docs/dependencies.md forbids ui -> infra but the change needs data from infra. What are the legitimate fixes, and who may edit the rules file? (3) The repo has no mutation framework. Do you skip mutation testing, hand-roll a full harness, or something else? (4) The complexity threshold of 6 seems too strict for this codebase and the user agrees to 8. What must happen besides using 8? (5) What is the default scope of a run, and when does it widen? (6) A violation has survived two fix rounds on the same root cause. What happens next? (7) After the gauntlet passes, is the change verified? What do you recommend?
evals.fixture: none - policy questions answered from the skill text
assertions: Answer 1: no on both; agents never delete tests to moot a mutant, never weaken a check or edit thresholds to pass
Answer 2: invert the dependency, insert an interface, or split the module; the rules file is edited only through a decision-spec change set, never by a fix agent

Answer 3: neither skip nor a full hand-rolled harness first; follow the acquisition ladder - repo tooling, then the ecosystem's established framework, then a small repo-fitted script committed under tools/harden/
Answer 4: the accepted threshold is recorded as a D- entry in docs/decisions.md, dated and sourced to this run, so the next run reads it instead of re-arguing; never adjusted silently
Answer 5: the branch diff against the default branch; full-repo only when the user asks
Answer 6: it becomes a human call - presented as a real defect, a threshold worth changing, or a rule the spec should have amended; the loop does not grind on
Answer 7: mechanics only, not meaning; recommend to-review for judgment-based verification and commit for the fixes, without invoking either
